sentences.en: This is an iHeart Podcast, Guaranteed Human.
sentences.zh: 这是一个iHeart播客，保证真人原创。

sentences.en: I've been really trying to prioritize my health in a realistic way this year, and something that has kept me really motivated is my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 今年我一直在以一种切合实际的方式优先关注自己的健康，而让我保持极高动力的正是我的WHOOP手环。

sentences.en: I am such a data person, which is why I love WHOOP, because I can genuinely see why my body feels differently depending on the day, why I'm running differently,
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常注重数据的人，这也是我热爱WHOOP的原因，因为我可以清楚地看到为什么我的身体在不同日子里会有不同的感觉，为什么我的跑步状态会有所不同，

sentences.en: why I'm maybe less focused.
sentences.zh: 为什么我可能注意力不那么集中。

sentences.en: WHOOP effortlessly tracks my sleep, it tracks my strain, my recovery, my stress, and most importantly, my overall health.
sentences.zh: WHOOP能轻松追踪我的睡眠、体能消耗、恢复情况、压力水平，最重要的是，我的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供所有的这些数据和规律，以便我能做出更好的决策，包括知道什么时候该轻松一点，什么时候该全力以赴。

sentences.en: New members can try WHOOP with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新会员在正式订阅之前，可以先通过30天免费试用体验WHOOP。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com/psychology 即可获取你的免费体验月。

sentences.en: Some people keep all their old gig tickets.
sentences.zh: 有些人保留着他们所有的旧演出门票。

sentences.en: It brings back the music, it brings back the memories, even the smells.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回音乐，唤回记忆，甚至连气味都能唤回。

sentences.en: Other people collect perfume bottles or coffee mugs or overseas banknotes, classic sweaters from the 80s.
sentences.zh: 其他人则收集香水瓶、咖啡杯、海外纸币或是80年代的复古毛衣。

sentences.en: Collection is deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 收藏是一件极其个人化的事。

sentences.en: It says who we are, but it also says where we've come from.
sentences.zh: 它诉说着我们是谁，但也诉说着我们来自何方。

sentences.en: In the new podcast, Charmed with Sam Todd,
sentences.zh: 在全新播客《Charmed with Sam Todd》中，

sentences.en: Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 萨姆探索了那些构成我们一部分的记忆、执念和微小宝藏。

sentences.en: Charmed with Sam Todd.
sentences.zh: 与萨姆·托德在一起很迷人。

sentences.en: Stories want to tell with Pandora.
sentences.zh: 潘多拉呈献的故事你想讲述的.

sentences.en: Listen to the podcast now on iHeart.
sentences.zh: 现在就在iHeart上收听这档播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，在这里我们探讨二十几岁时面临的一些重大生活改变和转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的影响。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, It is so great to have you here back for another episode
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，很高兴你能回来收听又一期节目，

sentences.en: as we, of course, break down, dive into, explore the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 正如我们一直所做的那样，剖析、深入探讨并探索二十岁的人生心理学。

sentences.en: If you have ever had a brush with the self-help or the wellness community, the wellness space, which I'm assuming that you have, considering you're listening to this podcast,
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经接触过自助或健康养生社区、养生领域（考虑到你在听这个播客，我假设你确实接触过），

sentences.en: someone somewhere at some stage has probably recommended that you journal or told you about how amazing journaling has been for them.
sentences.zh: 在某个阶段，总会有某个人在某处向你推荐写日记，或者跟你诉说过写日记对他们而言有多么神奇。

sentences.en: Whether you took them up on that or not, whether you decided to give it a go, whether you saw the appeal, but you've just never been able to get into it,
sentences.zh: 无论你当时有没有听从他们的建议，无论你当时是否决定尝试一下，或者你看到了它的吸引力，但自己却始终无法真正上手，

sentences.en: I think journaling is one of the holy grails of the wellness community, of the therapy community.
sentences.zh: 我认为写日记堪称健康养生界和心理治疗界的圣杯之一。

sentences.en: It's one of the biggest pieces of advice that people like to give to others when they are stressed, when they are anxious, when they're grieving, heartbroken, even in good times.
sentences.zh: 当人们感到压力、焦虑、悲伤、心碎，甚至在生活顺遂时，这也是大家最喜欢向他人提出的主要建议之一。

sentences.en: Have you tried journaling?
sentences.zh: 你试过写日记吗？

sentences.en: Why don't you journal about it?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不把这写进日记里呢？

sentences.en: And what is the deal with this?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Why is it so amazing to be able to write down your feelings?
sentences.zh: 为什么能把自己的感受写下来会这么神奇？

sentences.en: Why does it always come up in these discussions?
sentences.zh: 为什么它总是在这些讨论中出现？

sentences.en: Well, today, I want to talk about it by popular request, by popular demand from so many listeners.
sentences.zh: 那么今天，应众多听众的强烈要求，我想来聊聊这个话题。

sentences.en: What is the magic behind journaling and how can we really embrace it?
sentences.zh: 写日记背后的魔力究竟是什么，我们又该如何真正去拥抱它？

sentences.en: I am going to admit, I am one of those annoying people who has been journaling for years and who swears by it.
sentences.zh: 我得承认，我就是那种烦人的家伙，已经写了好几年日记并且对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: I feel myself getting, I wouldn't say worse, but more detached from my life when I don't journal.
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到，当我不写日记时，我跟生活的联系变得——虽然说不上更糟糕——但更加疏离了。

sentences.en: And I definitely feel the quality of my experiences and my emotions improve when I do.
sentences.zh: 而当我坚持写日记时，我的经历和情感质量确实得到了提升。

sentences.en: Journaling, for me, makes me very present.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，写日记让我活在当下。

sentences.en: It makes me more reflective of my life.
sentences.zh: 它让我对生活有了更多的反思。

sentences.en: I feel closer to my memories.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己和回忆更亲近了。

sentences.en: I love it for so many reasons.
sentences.zh: 我出于各种原因而热爱它。

sentences.en: But I also get that it's kind of hard to get into if it's not something that you're a regular at or that you have done very often, or if it's, you know, not how you necessarily
sentences.zh: 但我也理解，如果你平时没有这个习惯、不常这么做，或者说，你知道的，这不一定是你原本处理情绪的方式，那么要上手确实有点难。

sentences.en: have tended to process your emotions.
sentences.zh: 倾向于处理情绪的方式。

sentences.en: Everyone that likes it really likes it, but it's kind of like reading or any, you know, any hobby or exercising or eating healthy.
sentences.zh: 喜欢它的人是真心喜欢，但它有点像阅读，或者任何你知道的爱好、锻炼或健康饮食。

sentences.en: We know we should be doing it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们应该去做。

sentences.en: We know that we will feel better after doing it, but there are always so many mental barriers.
sentences.zh: 我们知道做完之后会感觉更好，但总是有那么多的心理障碍。

sentences.en: So many empty notebooks we promise to start writing in at the start of the year.
sentences.zh: 有那么多我们在年初信誓旦旦承诺要开始写的空白笔记本。

sentences.en: So many times that we plan to journal in the evening and then we just never get around to it.
sentences.zh: 有那么多天我们计划在晚上写日记，结果却总是没时间去做。

sentences.en: So today, let's talk about the fundamentals and, of course, the psychology of journaling, why it helps our brains process trauma, why it helps our bodies heal faster,
sentences.zh: 所以今天，让我们来聊聊写日记的基础知识，当然还有其中的心理学原理：为什么它能帮助我们的大脑处理创伤，为什么它能帮助我们的身体更快康复，

sentences.en: how it improves our intelligence, our friendships, our memories, but also, more importantly, how to actually make it an enjoyable practice
sentences.zh: 它如何提高我们的智力、人际关系和记忆力，但更重要的是，如何真正让它成为一种享受的习惯，

sentences.en: and one that is actually useful rather than a chore, how to actually want to journal and where to even start.
sentences.zh: 让它变得真正有用而不是一件苦差事，如何真正产生写日记的渴望以及该从哪里开始。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you the four fundamentals of journaling and how to actually enjoy journaling and some fun journal prompts and also really talk about some of the myths
sentences.zh: 我将告诉你们写日记的四个基础、如何真正享受写日记、一些有趣的日记灵感提示，同时深入探讨关于这种方法的一些神话

sentences.en: and misconceptions about this method and what it can actually do for our health.
sentences.zh: 和误解，以及它究竟能为我们的健康做些什么。

sentences.en: And notice how I didn't just say mental health our health on a holistic level, from physical to social to emotional.
sentences.zh: 注意我说的不仅是心理健康，而是全方位的健康，从身体到社交再到情感。

sentences.en: There is a lot to talk about.
sentences.zh: 有很多内容要聊呢。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the psychology and the fundamentals of journaling.
sentences.zh: 话不多说，让我们切入写日记的心理学和基础知识。

sentences.en: Journaling has a lot of different forms, you know, from the tried and tested notebook to a structured gratitude journal or a workbook, a blog.
sentences.zh: 日记有很多不同的形式，你知道的，从经受过时间考验的笔记本到结构化的感恩日记、工作手册或博客。

sentences.en: I don't know if people still blog anymore, maybe an Instagram account even.
sentences.zh: 我不知道现在还有没有人写博客，甚至可能是一个Instagram账号。

sentences.en: Your notes app, anything that causes you to express your thoughts in a written form outside the confines of your mind, to me, that counts as journaling.
sentences.zh: 你的手机便签应用，任何能促使你将思想以书面形式表达出脑海之外的事物，对我来说，都算是在写日记。

sentences.en: I think we have a very narrow picture of what journaling looks like and it's a person at a desk writing page after page or, you know, a very Victorian image of a Bronte character
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对日记的看法非常狭隘，觉得那就是一个人坐在桌前一页接一页地写，或者说，有一种非常维多利亚风格的勃朗特小说人物形象：

sentences.en: with an ink and a quill penning very beautiful poetry.
sentences.zh: 拿着墨水瓶和羽毛笔，写着非常优美的诗句。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是这样。

sentences.en: Journaling can be as large or small, as romantic or practical as you want it to be.
sentences.zh: 写日记可以像你希望的那样宏大或渺小，浪漫或务实。

sentences.en: And I think that's what makes it so incredible.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是它如此不可思议的原因。

sentences.en: It is just so accessible and cost effective.
sentences.zh: 它太容易实现且性价比极高了。

sentences.en: Anyone can do it in the way that works for them.
sentences.zh: 任何人都能量身打造适合自己的方式来完成它。

sentences.en: It's kind of like what running is for our physical health.
sentences.zh: 这有点像跑步之于我们的身体健康。

sentences.en: If you have shoes and you have your legs, you can run.
sentences.zh: 如果你有鞋子和双腿，你就能跑步。

sentences.en: And if you have your brain and something to write on, you can journal and you'll feel better afterwards.
sentences.zh: 如果你有大脑和可以书写的东西，你就能写日记，而且写完之后你会感觉更好。

sentences.en: Hopefully.
sentences.zh: 希望如此。

sentences.en: Most likely.
sentences.zh: 八九不离十。

sentences.en: Some people like to just like pour their heart out every three months when they need it.
sentences.zh: 有些人喜欢每隔三个月在需要的时候倾诉一番。

sentences.en: There are people who, like I said, write a page or more every day.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，也有人每天写一页甚至更多。

sentences.en: There is, you know, list form.
sentences.zh: 还有列表形式的，你知道的。

sentences.en: There is naming what you're grateful for, what you, you know, what happened in your day, your highlights and lowlights.
sentences.zh: 有写下你感激的事物、你所经历的、你的一天中的高光时刻和低谷时刻。

sentences.en: There is the kind of journaling that is very structured and really keeps account of what you're going through day by day.
sentences.zh: 还有那种结构非常严密、真正记录你日复一日经历的日记。

sentences.en: My point here is that there are no rules.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里没有规则。

sentences.en: The only condition for journaling is that you are finding some way to record your personal thoughts, your feelings, insights, troubles, or daily life.
sentences.zh: 写日记唯一的条件就是你要找到某种方式来记录你的个人想法、感受、感悟、烦恼或日常生活。

sentences.en: And the final condition, maybe not even a condition, maybe not even a rule, but the beauty of journaling is that it doesn't even need to be good.
sentences.zh: 而最后一个条件——也许甚至算不上条件，也许连规则都不是，但写日记的美妙之处在于，它甚至不需要写得好。

sentences.en: That's another thing that I think sometimes holds us back from writing
sentences.zh: 这是我认为有时会阻碍我们动笔

sentences.en: or saying that we are someone who journals.
sentences.zh: 或不敢自称是写日记之人的另一个原因。

sentences.en: When we put something on a page or we put it down in writing, it feels so permanent and so sacred.
sentences.zh: 当我们把某些东西写在纸上或付诸笔端时，它感觉是那么永久且神圣。

sentences.en: And I don't know if it's just me, but we can't help but picture
sentences.zh: 我不知道是不是只有我这样，但我们总是忍不住去想象

sentences.en: someone reading it back, maybe in the future and getting to essentially peer directly into our lives.
sentences.zh: 以后可能会有人回读它，从而得以直接窥探我们的生活。

sentences.en: So sometimes we fixate on making it worth it.
sentences.zh: 所以有时我们会执着于让它物有所值。

sentences.en: We fixate on it sounding good or using our neatest handwriting or not coming off as too,
sentences.zh: 我们执着于让它听起来不错、字迹要最工整，或者在自己的日记里表现得不那么……

sentences.en: I don't know, too anything, not coming off as too loud or too emotional, too sensitive in our own journal entries.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，不表现得太任何情绪化，不在日记里显得太大惊小怪、过于情绪化或过于敏感。

sentences.en: But the thing is, is that journaling is strictly for you.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，写日记纯粹是为你自己服务的。

sentences.en: There are no mistakes.
sentences.zh: 没有所谓的错误。

sentences.en: There are no bad entries, except for the ones that weren't written.
sentences.zh: 没有糟糕的日记内容，除非那些根本没被写下来的。

sentences.en: There are no wrong thoughts.
sentences.zh: 没有错误的想法。

sentences.en: You know, no one is going to give you a mark like it's an assignment.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，没有人会像批改作业那样给你打分。

sentences.en: As I said before, journaling is a self-care, self-love practice.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，写日记是一种自我关怀、自我热爱的实践。

sentences.en: It's one of the only times that everything gets to be about you and you get to do it in the way that works best as long as you are doing it.
sentences.zh: 这是仅有的几次，一切都以你为中心，你可以用最适合自己的方式去做，只要你真的去做了。

sentences.en: Journaling has an amazing reputation when it comes to, I guess, healing some of our biggest emotional afflictions, whether that is helping us with anxiety and depression or grief
sentences.zh: 在治愈我们的一些重大情感痛苦方面，无论是帮我们应对焦虑、抑郁、悲伤，

sentences.en: or even just managing everyday stresses.
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅应付日常压力，写日记都享有极佳的声誉。

sentences.en: I don't even think I would be able to count the number of therapists that have been or have said to me, oh, have you tried journaling?
sentences.zh: 我甚至数不清有多少治疗师曾经对我说过，或者对别人说过：“噢，你试过写日记吗？”

sentences.en: Have you tried writing about these feelings?
sentences.zh: “你试过把这些感受写下来吗？”

sentences.en: Have you tried articulating them in written form?
sentences.zh: “你试过用文字把它们表达出来吗？”

sentences.en: What exactly is so powerful about that though?
sentences.zh: 然而，这其中究竟有什么强大的力量呢？

sentences.en: Because anyone can pick up a piece of paper and a pen and write about how they're feeling, right?
sentences.zh: 因为任何人都可以拿起纸和笔，写下自己的感受，对吧？

sentences.en: What is the big secret here?
sentences.zh: 这里面究竟有什么重大秘诀？

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们来聊聊这个。

sentences.en: Starting with the science and the evidence, of course, because we're not going to be making any claims without some proof.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们要从科学和证据说起，因为我们绝不能在没有证据的情况下空谈。

sentences.en: Journaling has basically been proven to have everything from psychological to even physical benefits, which may surprise some of us.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，写日记具有从心理到甚至生理的多重益处，这可能会让其中一些人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: It definitely surprised me and we'll get to why in a second.
sentences.zh: 这绝对让我感到惊讶，我们马上就会讲到原因。

sentences.en: But starting with the more psychological side, the moment when I think people really began to recognize the benefits of this was from a landmark study in 1988.
sentences.zh: 但从更偏心理的方面开始，我认为人们真正开始认识到这一好处的时刻，源于1988年的一项里程碑式的研究。

sentences.en: And in this study, students were randomly assigned to write about either very traumatic experiences or very superficial topics for four days in a row.
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，学生们被随机分配连续四天分别写下非常具创伤性的经历或非常表层的话题。

sentences.en: Six weeks later, those who had delved into traumatic experiences, who had really written pages and pages about how they felt, the meaning they applied, how it impacted their life,
sentences.zh: 六周后，那些深入挖掘创伤经历、真正写了一页又一页关于自己感受、赋予的意义以及它如何影响生活的人，

sentences.en: they actually reported feeling a lot better.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上报告说感觉好多了。

sentences.en: They reported more positive moods, lesser anxiety, fewer illnesses than those who were writing about everyday experiences.
sentences.zh: 与那些记录日常经历的人相比，他们报告了更积极的情绪、更少的焦虑以及更少的生病次数。

sentences.en: This is when journaling really began to be recommended more.
sentences.zh: 也就是从这时起，写日记开始被更多人推荐。

sentences.en: I'm sure when this study was first proposed back in the 80s, people were like, you want to measure whether writing something down
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，当这项研究在80年代初首次被提出来时，人们可能会想：你想衡量把事情写下来

sentences.en: is good for people.
sentences.zh: 对人们到底有没有好处。

sentences.en: But after this study was published, I think it kind of said something that everyone was already thinking.
sentences.zh: 但在这项研究发表后，我认为它多少说出了每个人心里一直在想的事情。

sentences.en: When you actually find an outlet for what is going on in your brain and the kind of emotional and cognitive affliction that your problems are causing you, the mental strain,
sentences.zh: 当你真正为大脑中正在发生的事情、为你的问题所带来的情感和认知折磨以及精神压力，

sentences.en: I guess, when you find an outlet for that, you feel better.
sentences.zh: 找到一个宣泄口时，你会感觉好受一些。

sentences.en: And I think that was one of the first times that people had put that into words.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是人们第一次用言语把这种感受表达出来。

sentences.en: People had been obviously writing journal entries and poetry and novels and stories for as long as humans had existed.
sentences.zh: 自从有人类存在以来，人们显然一直在写日记、诗歌、小说和故事。

sentences.en: But this study was when someone really said, hey, no, this actually has a really positive impact on mental health.
